themes.title: The repricing of AI capital: mega-funds meet margin discipline
themes.summary: Markets are repricing the risk of AI buildout financing. DBS' CEO says investors are demanding more discipline, Bloomberg reports the AI boom is now a major force in corporate credit with rising concentration, and finance chiefs are tightening budgets as costs climb - even as SoftBank's Masayoshi Son seeks a fresh $100 billion after putting $65 billion into OpenAI.
themes.angle: Capital, not technology, is becoming the binding constraint on the AI buildout.

themes.title: World Bank: UAE and Jordan carry the Middle East's biggest AI job risk
themes.summary: A World Bank assessment ranks the UAE and Jordan as the Middle East's most AI-exposed labour markets by share of jobs at risk. The finding cuts against the region's self-image of AI leadership and puts workforce transition on the board agenda, alongside Emiratisation and GCC talent strategy.
themes.angle: AI leadership claims meet workforce reality - the Gulf's exposure cuts both ways.

themes.title: GCC AI diplomacy: a UAE-US axis firms up while China beckons
themes.summary: The UAE and US held talks to deepen cooperation on AI, quantum and space, while 16 Emirati AI experts are set to tour China's AI ecosystem. Abu Dhabi's transition continues to be framed as a sovereign strategy, and Dubai Police have set AI-powered operations targets to 2033 as the UAE claims a top global AI-integration ranking.
themes.angle: The region is hedging its AI partnerships across both superpowers - an executive-grade geopolitical signal.

themes.title: Consolidation: value migrates from models to distribution and compute
themes.summary: Amazon is in talks to acquire Decart - the WSJ-reported deal could be worth around $7 billion, one of the biggest AI acquisitions in discussion. As capabilities commoditize, Microsoft's Jacob Andreou warns of a product gap, and an 'AI paradox' argues cheaper tokens make compute itself more valuable.
themes.angle: Hyperscalers are buying the AI stack rather than building it - and compute, not models, captures the value.

themes.title: Frontier chatter: singularity claims, small models, voice and medicine

High-speed product cadence, uneven evidence.
themes.angle: Hype claims and shipped products are diverging - verify before you budget.

themes.title: The physical layer: mobility, hardware and the talent war
themes.summary: Xpeng says its driver-assist systems can adapt to European roads with small data; Apple supplier Luxshare faces a US patent probe over data-center power tech; Apple's smart-home line launches this week; and DeepMind is advertising high-paying research roles that require no degree. Hardware supply chains and skills pull in opposite directions.
themes.angle: Physical-layer economics and the no-degree talent pivot are both board-level signals.
